literature_notes: The ledger contains two lines (L1, L2) both describing the same FCRL3-TM-GFP chimeric construct. In that construct the FCRL3 ectodomain (residues 18–576) is fused in-frame to a heterologous transmembrane region and a cytoplasmic GFP. Three disqualifying features prevent any surface-tag site from being derived: (1) The GFP is on the intracellular face, not the extracellular face, so it cannot ground an extracellular tag site. (2) No tag is inserted at a specific residue within the FCRL3 ectodomain; the ectodomain is displayed intact and unmodified. (3) The surface confirmation in L2 rests on anti-FCRL3 antibody staining of unpermeabilized cells, which is antibody epitope mapping and is explicitly excluded as evidence for an insertion site. The construct is also a chimera (heterologous TM), not a full-length native FCRL3 with a tag knocked in. Because no ledger line reports a tolerated epitope-tag, fluorescent-protein, transposon, or domain insertion at any specific extracellular residue or loop of full-length membrane-anchored FCRL3, zero sites qualify. The cytoplasmic GFP junction is recorded in other_positions.

literature_other_positions.note: In the FCRL3-TM-GFP chimera the GFP is fused on the cytoplasmic side of a heterologous TM appended after the FCRL3 ectodomain (which ends at residue 576 in the native protein); the GFP is intracellular and does not constitute an extracellular tag insertion.
